from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: The Seven Bridges of Königsberg", 
                          ["Euler solved the Seven Bridges of Konigsberg problem.", 
                           "He reduced the city to a graph diagram.", 
                           "This birthed the field of graph theory."])
        
        # Load Assets
        river = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/river.svg")
        bridge = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bridge.svg")
        
        # Create Graph for Konigsberg
        nodes = {1: [0, 1, 0], 2: [2, 1, 0], 3: [1, 0, 0], 4: [1, 2, 0]}
        edges = [(1, 4), (1, 4), (1, 3), (1, 3), (2, 4), (2, 4), (2, 3)]
        graph = Graph(nodes.keys(), edges, layout=nodes, labels=True)
        graph_label = Text("Königsberg Graph", font_size=20)
        
        self.place_in_area(graph, "B3", "E5", scale_factor=0.75)
        self.place_at_grid(graph_label, "D2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(river), Create(graph))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight bridges
        for edge in graph.edges:
             graph.edges[edge].add(bridge.copy().scale(0.5).move_to(graph.edges[edge].get_center()))
        self.play(graph.animate.set_color(RED), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Trace path (simplistic highlighting)
        path = VGroup(*[graph.edges[edge] for edge in edges])
        self.play(Indicate(path), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: Why it Matters", [
            "Topology informs modern data analysis and robotics.",
            "It even helps us understand the universe's shape.",
            "Topology connects abstract math to reality."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a collection of diverse topological structures
        robot = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg")
        shapes = VGroup(
            Torus(major_radius=0.5, minor_radius=0.2, color=BLUE),
            Sphere(radius=0.4, color=RED),
            robot
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(shapes, 'A2', 'B5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(shapes))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Morph them into each other smoothly in #FFFFFF
        new_shapes = VGroup(
            Sphere(radius=0.4, color=WHITE),
            Torus(major_radius=0.5, minor_radius=0.2, color=WHITE),
            robot.copy().set_color(WHITE)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(new_shapes, 'C2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Transform(shapes, new_shapes))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(RED)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show a final text 'Topology is everywhere' in gold (#FFD700) featuring a globe.svg

sections.title: The Hook: What is Topology?
sections.content: Introduce topology as 'rubber-sheet geometry.' Explain that in topology, distance and angles don't matter—only connectivity and continuity remain. If you can deform an object into another without tearing or gluing, they are topologically equivalent (homeomorphic).
sections.example: An animation showing a coffee mug being smoothly stretched and morphed into a donut (torus) while keeping the handle hole intact.

sections.title: The Golden Rule: Invariants
sections.content: Define 'Invariants'—properties that stay the same despite continuous deformation. Focus on the 'Genus' (the number of holes). Explain that a sphere has 0 holes, a torus has 1, and a pretzel has 3. These numbers distinguish shapes regardless of how they are stretched.
sections.example: Visualizing a balloon character (0 holes) vs. a physical whistle (1 hole); showing that no matter how much you squeeze the balloon, it can never become the whistle.

sections.title: The Classic Proof: Euler's Characteristic
sections.content: Introduce the formula V - E + F = 2. Vertices (V), Edges (E), and Faces (F). Explain that for any convex polyhedron, this value is constant. This is the bridge between rigid geometry and flexible topology.
sections.example: A 3D cube counting exercise: 8 vertices - 12 edges + 6 faces = 2. Then, showing how this holds true even if the cube is 'dented' or distorted.

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Seven Bridges of Königsberg
sections.content: Briefly mention how Leonhard Euler solved the problem of crossing seven bridges exactly once by treating the landmasses as 'nodes' and bridges as 'lines.' This birthed Graph Theory, a branch of topology.
sections.example: A map of Königsberg where the city layout transforms into a simple point-and-line diagram, proving the journey is impossible.

sections.title: Conclusion: Why it Matters
sections.content: Summarize that topology is the foundation of modern data analysis, robotics path planning, and even understanding the shape of the universe.
sections.example: A quick visual montage of a robot arm calculating its path (topology) and a map of a neural network connection.
